verdictWhy: I built the whole evening in one sitting and the run went as the notes ask, so yes, I could tour on this. But twice it frightened me: my tracks vanished until I saved, and the house fade showed no fade until I typed in a level it already seemed to have. I would rehearse every cue before trusting it in front of an audience.

tasks.notes: Seven files added in one go, but the list stayed empty until I saved the show; numbers typed then Tab were lost and had to be redone with Enter.
Loop found on the Audio tab after looking in Time & Loops. The fade cue needed its target chosen and its To level typed before it reported a real fade.
Start at 12, End at 40, Fade out 5 on one line; duration became 0:28.0 and it played from 0:12. I could not check the fade-out itself (rig).
auto-follow plus Post-wait 3; confirmed in the run: 3 seconds of silence, then Lantern with no GO.
Level -4 on the Audio tab; plays at -4.0 dB. Not visible in the list.
Saved as Tides tour.ecshow on the desk (it copies the music in). Reopening the app brought the show back exactly.
Load to Time 0:30, GO, stop, and again. Works only in Edit mode.

Show mode locked delete and rename. House loop, 8 s out, Tide, Salt at -4, Undertow from 0:12, Driftwood into Lantern, Bows all sounded as expected; moved on with the Active cues bar "Click to skip there".
No Help menu; found Settings > Keys: GO Space, Panic Esc (again: stop dead), playhead ↑ ↓.

findings.title: Sounds added to a new, unsaved show do not appear in the cue list until the show is saved
findings.expected: After New show > Audio > choosing seven files, seven cues in the list, as QLab does on an untitled workspace.
findings.happened: The top bar said "7 unsaved" and Undo read "Undo add 7 sounds", but the list still said "No cues yet" and the footer "0 cues". A second try with one file gave "8 unsaved", still "No cues yet". Only after Save (to a folder on the desk) did all eight rows appear at once, including the duplicate "01 Tide-2" I then had to delete. Nothing on screen said a save was needed.
findings.steps: Start the app. New show. Click ♪ Audio, choose any wav. Look at the list: "No cues yet", chip says "1 unsaved". Save the show to a folder: the cue appears. (Seen twice in one session: 7 files, then 1 file.)
findings.suggestion: Show the cues at once in an unsaved show, or ask for a folder before the first sound is added.

findings.title: A Fade cue with To level left as the grey "-inf" does not fade: it holds the level, then cuts
findings.expected: The To level box shows "-inf", so I took it as already set to fade to silence over my 8 seconds.
findings.happened: With target House music, Duration 0:08.00, Stop target when done on, and To level untouched, `hear` reported "House music at 0.0 dB (fading to NaN dB)" through the whole 8 seconds, then "Silence." After I typed -inf into the box myself it reported "fading to -60 dB". I cannot hear the rig, so I am not certain the sound really stays at full level, but the target is "NaN" until the box is typed in.
findings.steps: Add an audio cue, add a Fade, choose the audio cue as Target, set Duration 8, leave To level alone. GO the audio, GO the fade, hear: "fading to NaN dB". (Run three times.)
findings.suggestion: Make the shown -inf the real default value.

findings.title: A cue Number typed and left with Tab is thrown away, and the old text stays in the box for the next cue
findings.expected: Type the number, Tab to Name, type the name: both kept. That is how every form works.
findings.happened: Typed 0, Tab, typed "House music", Enter. The name was kept, the NUMBER column stayed blank though the box still read "0". Selecting the next cue and typing 1 made the box read "01"; again nothing in the list. Typing the number and pressing Enter does keep it.
findings.steps: Select a cue, click Number in Basics, type 1, press Tab. The list shows no number. Select another cue: the Number box still shows the 1. (Twice: cue 0 and cue 1.)
findings.suggestion: Keep a field's value when it loses the keyboard.

findings.title: The row of the cue that is playing shrinks to a small tag at the left edge of the list
findings.expected: The playing cue stays a full row, marked as playing, so I can see where I am in the running order.
findings.happened: With Bows playing in Show mode its row was a small box reading only "Bows" at the far left, with no number or time, where the other rows are full width. Seen in one picture; in the text the live row always sat at x=17 instead of with the others, so it may be every time.
findings.steps: Open a show in Show mode, GO the last cue, look at its row.

findings.title: Clicking the middle of a Fade row with no name does not select it; the inspector stays on the previous cue
findings.expected: A click anywhere on a row selects that cue and the inspector shows it.
findings.happened: I clicked the Fade row in its name area and went to the inspector to type the level. The inspector was still Tide's, and my "-inf" went into Tide's File box: "Its file is missing." Clicking the row near its left edge did select it. The unnamed Fade row shows an open name box that swallows the click.
findings.steps: Add a Fade and leave it unnamed. Select another cue. Click the Fade row around the NAME column. The inspector does not change.

findings.title: Load to Time does nothing in Show mode and says nothing
findings.expected: Picking a track up from a time is a rehearsal thing I do with the show locked; or else a word saying it is not available.
findings.happened: In Show mode ⌘T and Tools > Load to Time… opened no bar and showed no message; only the footer "SHOW MODE — editing is locked". In Edit mode the same command works.
findings.steps: Switch to Show. Select an audio cue. Tools > Load to Time…. Nothing appears. (Tried by key and by menu.)
findings.suggestion: Allow it in Show mode, or grey the menu item.

findings.title: There is no Help menu; the keys are under Settings > Keys
findings.expected: A Help menu, or a ? on the window, with the keys and a link to the manual.
findings.happened: The menu bar is App, File, Edit, View, Tools, Window. I found the list by opening the ⚙ and trying "Keys". The list itself is good: "GO Space", "Panic (again: stop dead) Esc", "Move the playhead ↑ ↓". There is no entry called "back one cue"; I took ↑ to be it.
findings.steps: Look through the menu bar for help.
findings.suggestion: Add a Help menu with Keys and the getting-started page.

findings.title: Loop is on the Audio tab, not on the tab called Time & Loops
findings.happened: Time & Loops has a waveform, Markers and "Loop regions: None. A region is a stretch that loops cleanly…" with no button to make one and no plain loop switch. The Loop switch is on the Audio tab. Once on, the row gets a clear "loop" tag.
findings.steps: Select an audio cue, open Time & Loops.

findings.title: A new Fade has no target though it was added with the sound selected
findings.expected: QLab targets the cue I had selected.
findings.happened: The Fade came in with ✕ and "No target."; I chose "0 · House music" from the list. Clear enough, one extra step. Choosing it also moved every field up a line, so my next click missed.
findings.steps: Select an audio cue, click ◢ Fade.

findings.title: The toolbar offers 17 kinds of cue, drawn so dim they look switched off
findings.expected: The three or four I know (Audio, Fade, Stop) easy to see.
findings.happened: Group, Audio, Fade, Stop, Start, Pause, Devamp, Load, GoTo, Arm, Disarm, Wait, Memo, Network, Light, Mix, Jump in dark grey on dark brown. "Devamp", "Arm", "Network" and "Jump" are not my words.
findings.steps: New show; look at the toolbar.

findings.title: A cue's level is not shown in the list, and a follow is only a small arrow
findings.expected: To see from the list that Salt is at -4 and that Driftwood goes on by itself.
findings.happened: Salt's -4 dB is only in the inspector's Audio tab (and in Active cues once it plays). Driftwood shows "0:03.0" and a ⤓; standing by on it says "then 5 · Lantern" with no word that Lantern follows without a GO.
findings.steps: Set a level and an auto-follow; look at the list in Show mode.

findings.title: In Show mode a click on a row still moves the playhead, and Reset sits beside Panic
findings.expected: Locked means a stray click cannot change what GO does next.
findings.happened: Show mode did stop Backspace deleting and double-click renaming. But one click on Undertow made it the standing-by cue, and "Reset" ("Stop everything; playhead to the top") is one button below Panic with no confirm that I saw. The mixer knobs stay live too.

findings.title: Load to Time is exactly what a dancer's "from 0:30" needs
findings.expected: To fiddle with the cue's start time and have to put it back.
findings.happened: Tools > Load to Time… (⌘T), typed 0:30, Enter: "LOADED TO 0:30.0" by Standing by; GO played Salt from 0:30 at -4 dB. The second time took four keys. It does not remember 0:30 from the last time.

findings.title: The standing-by line and the save chip say what will happen
findings.happened: "Standing by 0 House music — then House out" in large type; "9 unsaved" with the list of what; after saving "Saved v2 — … House out added …"; reopening the app brought the show back as left, playhead at the top. The ↺ "Put back to media/01 Tide.wav" rescued a field I had wrecked.

findings.title: Auto-follow with a post-wait did what the choreographer asked, first time
findings.happened: Continue: auto-follow, Post-wait 3 on Driftwood. In the run: Driftwood ended, "Lantern is waiting (0:02.3 of 0:03.0)", then Lantern played. Start at / End at / Fade out for Undertow were three boxes on one line and the row's duration became 0:28.0.

rig: `hear` shows a cue's set level, not where a fade-out inside the cue has got to, so Undertow's 5-second fade out could not be checked.
I ran well over the 150 actions (about 390 journal lines with looks, waits and hears): several clicks were sent in batches by position and missed after the layout moved, and had to be redone.
The run was stopped and restarted once before the first task (the show's own app was open; the owner's go-ahead was relayed).
